conversation.text: Hi, thanks for calling Korami Sushi. What would you like to order?
Hi, yeah, I'd like to place an order for pickup.
Great, I can help with that. What would you like to order?
Can I get two orders of the Spicy Tuna Crispy Rice, and one Dragon Roll?
Two Spicy Tuna Crispy Rice and one Dragon Roll. Got it. Anything else?
Actually, can you make the Dragon Roll with soy paper instead of seaweed? I have a seaweed allergy.
I've noted the seaweed allergy, and I've updated the Dragon Roll to use soy paper. Is there anything else you'd like to add?
Your total is $42.50. Can I get a name for the order?
Thanks Alex. Your order is confirmed, and I've texted you the details. Goodbye!

steps.title: Customer Calls

faq.title: How KOTA Works in Practice
faq.subtitle: We don't promise magic. We promise a reliable operational tool. Here is exactly how KOTA works in practice.

items.question: Does KOTA work with my current menu?
items.answer: Yes. KOTA does not require a POS integration. We build your menu data from your menu PDFs, text, or photos. If you have complex modifiers or combos, we review the logic by hand before any live call.

items.question: How do orders get sent to my staff?
items.answer: Today, each order is saved as a structured record and the caller receives a text confirmation. Getting orders to your kitchen (by printer, tablet, or a text to staff) is not built yet; we set that up with each pilot restaurant.

items.question: Can it answer common questions about our restaurant?
items.answer: KOTA answers menu questions from the menu data we onboard. Hours, parking, and other general questions are on the roadmap.

items.question: What happens if a customer asks something KOTA doesn't know?
items.answer: KOTA answers only from your menu data. If it can't find a match, it offers real menu items instead of guessing, and the caller can press 0 at any time to reach your staff.

items.question: What cuisines or restaurant types are a good fit?
items.answer: KOTA is a tested prototype and we are looking for our first pilot restaurants: high-volume takeout businesses where missed calls mean lost revenue, especially Pizza, Sushi, Thai, Chinese, and busy fast-casual concepts.
